title: The Kindly Winter
premise: Folklorist Juniper Fairweather arrives in the snowbound village of Hollowmere to record its carols, only to find every song ends mid-verse, as if the singers are afraid of what comes after. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old chapel, the village's silence breaks: in 1974, the townspeople gave one of their own to what lives below, and the thing they bound has been counting winters ever since. As villagers begin sleepwalking toward the dig site and her recordings play back verses no one sang aloud, Juniper discovers her own grandmother was the woman who performed the sealing — and that the debt passes down the bloodline. In the end, Juniper descends alone through the door, returning not the stolen relic but the truth of the victim's name, sung at last; the village is freed, but she stays below as the new keeper, writing letters that arrive each winter with no postmark.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from villages that no longer exist on any map. She writes in unheated rooms because, she claims, cold keeps the sentences honest.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't Sung
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere during the first snowfall, recording elderly singers whose carols all break off at the same line. The villagers are warm but evasive; her landlady burns a tape rather than let it be played twice. Emotional beat: creeping unease beneath cozy hospitality, as documentation starts to feel like trespass.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Alternating between Juniper and dig foreman Callum Rook. The crew breaches a door beneath the chapel — bolted shut from within — and finds a child's shoe, a 1974 newspaper, and scratch marks on the far side. That night, Juniper's recorder captures humming in an empty room. Emotional beat: dread hardening into certainty that the village buried something alive.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She finds her late grandmother's journal among the chapel records: the 1974 rite, the chosen girl's name deliberately erased, the bargain renewed each solstice. Villagers begin sleepwalking toward the open door, and the erased name appears in Juniper's own handwriting while she sleeps. Emotional beat: love against duty, as she realizes her bloodline owes the debt.

chapters.title: The Kindly Winter
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, closing with Callum's epilogue letter. On the solstice night she descends through the door, sings the victim's true name — Edith Marlowe — into the dark, and trades herself for the village's release. The door seals again, this time from the outside. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into justice, and the terrible peace of a debt finally paid.
